corroboration_exceptions.reason: These are claims about Climate Interactive's own model structure and licensing boundaries. The publisher is the source of record; separate official pages or chapters were checked, and outside descriptions would not be independent evidence of implementation details or license terms.

These exact latest-year estimates originate in the IEA's 2026 assessment. Separate report chapters were checked. Other compilers either use different methods or do not publish an exactly comparable value; the corpus preserves those differences instead of treating them as direct corroboration.

IRENA is the source of record for the exact technology-by-technology year-end renewable-capacity table. Comparable third-party totals have different technology and quality-flag definitions. Each component was rechecked in its separate IRENA table and the unit conversion is recorded.

EIA is the U.S. federal statistical source of record for these exact production, consumption, generation, flow, and storage-accounting values. Independent tables, survey programs, or diagrams within EIA were checked; external summaries generally reproduce EIA rather than independently measure the national totals.

These are exact claims about EPA's own legal-action status and scope at the recorded verification date. EPA is the source of record; third-party descriptions would not be independent evidence of agency status. Both claims carry high update risk, explicit proposal/final or partial-repeal boundaries, and mandatory reverification rules.

These are exact values or structural facts from the publisher's own statistical table or model. The source of record was checked in at least two publisher-controlled representations where available, and raw cells/API responses were independently revalidated. An external source would generally reproduce rather than independently measure the same modeled or estimated values. Cross-source comparisons are retained separately instead of being presented as exact corroboration.

known_limits: This is an exhaustive source-and-method review, not a redistribution of every row in every underlying dataset.
Several authoritative 2025 totals are preliminary and will be revised by their publishers.
IEA and Energy Institute global totals can differ because of estimation timing and primary-energy accounting methods.
The En-ROADS public documentation is sufficient for an architecture-compatible clean-room specification, not a verified bit-for-bit clone of the production simulator.
U.S.-specific AEO and ReEDS scenario series end in 2050; the corpus does not extrapolate U.S. values to 2070.
Global marine-energy scenario coverage is a sparse IRENA WETO milestone series ending in 2050; no marine-specific 2070 value is asserted.
The impact matrix identifies pathways and tradeoffs; it is not a site-specific impact assessment or a single technology ranking.
Quantitative mortality, land, water, material, waste, cost, and reliability calculations remain disabled until a compatible, configuration-specific coefficient ledger is built.
U.S. regulatory status is a federal baseline as of 2026-08-01, not legal advice or a complete state, Tribal, local, regional-market, or project permit inventory.
The NRC and EIA official operating-reactor counts conflict; both values and dates are preserved.
The demand package contains annual energy volumes, not hourly load shapes; it cannot by itself establish peak demand, ramping, resource adequacy, or transmission requirements.
AEO data-center values isolate server electricity, while IEA and LBNL milestones use total-facility definitions; the two scopes are not spliced.
The EIA MER EV series is experimental, changes method beginning in 2023, and is already included in electricity sales and use.
The 2018 NREL Electrification Futures Study is retained as an electrification stress test, not a current forecast.
